state.verified_context: FAIL-R03 for Can Rust compiler LSP transport. read_message currently read_until newline into unbounded header vectors, accepts ignored headers including a tested 2 MiB line and 8192 short headers, then vec![0; declared length] before reading body. Existing MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES=64 MiB enforced before allocation; accepted declared 64 MiB with no payload gives Read a 67,108,864-byte output buffer. Existing actual VS Code client writes one Content-Length CRLF header using UTF-8 byte count; server writer same. Reader tolerates case-insensitive Content-Length, bare LF, trimmed decimal lengths, unknown extension headers, and last duplicate length wins. run_stdio currently continues on framing errors in the same server state without proven resync, stops EOF/torn frames using existing lifecycle exit code, and emits JSON-RPC parse error for invalid JSON/UTF8 in correctly framed complete bodies. Ordinary request envelope/lifecycle has separate tested admission. Tests can use 64 KiB headers, declared-body/no-payload and observed reader buffers, finite stdio transcripts; no exhaustion experiments. User authorizes necessary support choices; scoped owner only framing/stdio closure/tests.
state.normative_context: Microsoft primary LSP 3.17 and 3.18 specs define required Content-Length as content bytes, ASCII header fields separated by colon-space and CRLF, UTF-8 content; no numeric frame/header budgets, duplicate-length handling or malformed framing recovery recipe specified. 3.17 says header fields conform to HTTP semantic. Content-Type UTF-8 defaults and utf8 legacy are valid; transport ignores other headers (unchanged). Budgets are local supported admission choices, not language source limits or claimed normative LSP maxima.
state.outcomes: Bound retained framing memory before validation; preserve ordinary client, legal extension headers and exact byte boundaries/partial reads; terminate untrusted framing without accidentally dispatching embedded payload as new messages; narrow ownership/simple implementation; avoid introducing generic framework/source restrictions. Larger headers have more compatibility room, smaller stricter budgets lower worst-case retained bytes; finite aggregate budget alone also bounds per-line/count without additional knobs. Geometric fallible body growth capped by accepted declared length gives no declared-size preallocation with no bytes and proportional growth when bytes actually arrive. No time deadline/slow-client policy requested.

budget.instructions: Which released local header/body admission policy best fits the verified ordinary peers and finite resource objective?

criteria.64k_incremental: Set 64 KiB aggregate wire header budget including terminator; retain existing 64 MiB body ceiling; use bounded fill_buf acquisitions and fallible geometric Vec growth only once bytes arrive, capped by declared length. No separate line/count policy.
criteria.16k_incremental: Set 16 KiB aggregate wire header budget including terminator with same existing body cap and arrived-byte growth. Stricter memory, less headroom for unknown extensions.
criteria.framework: Adopt a broader LSP/JSON-RPC transport framework with its own resource/lifecycle policy; qualify ordinary peers and extension support before release. More machinery but potentially reusable policy and less handwritten code.
criteria.body_only: Keep unbounded header parsing for compatibility, fix only premature body allocation. Preserves all current headers but leaves confirmed retained-header resource gap.

duplicates.instructions: Which duplicate Content-Length rule offers the clearest byte boundary and compatibility tradeoff?

criteria.same_only: Accept repeated Content-Length only when parsed decimal byte counts are equal, including case variations/leading zeros; reject disagreement, invalid value, or any oversized declaration. Preserves unambiguous duplicates while removing last-wins ambiguity.
criteria.single_only: Reject every duplicate Content-Length, even equal values; simplest unique-declaration rule but removes unambiguous duplicate compatibility.
criteria.last_wins: Preserve existing last-valid-length wins including disagreements; maximizes compatibility but inconsistent declarations can change the frame boundary.

malformed_lifecycle.instructions: How should actual stdio handle malformed framing after initialization, compared with complete-body JSON errors?

criteria.close_failure: Any non-EOF framing/I/O failure ends stdio with exit 1, no JSON-RPC reply because request/body unknown; flush prior outputs. EOF/torn frame retains current lifecycle exit behavior; correctly framed invalid JSON/UTF8 remains one parse-error response and subsequent frames continue.
criteria.close_lifecycle: End stdio on every non-EOF framing/I/O error using current lifecycle exit code (often 0) and flush prior outputs. Complete-body JSON/UTF8 parse errors still reply and continue.
criteria.continue: Keep serving the same stream/server after InvalidData, as today, treating subsequent bytes as fresh headers. Retains opportunistic recovery but body bytes may be reinterpreted and boundary/state reset is not assured.
criteria.resync: Implement scanning or draining/resynchronization with documented budget and state-reset rules, then continue. Could preserve connections but requires a larger framing design and proof of boundary detection.
